concept: Gemma 4 sliding-window layer exclusion from KV quantization
summary: vLLM documents that some attention layer types, e.g. sliding-window, are more sensitive to KV-cache quantization and provides `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` to leave chosen layers at native dtype while the rest use the quantized dtype.

facts.text: vLLM documents that some attention layer types, e.g. sliding-window, are more sensitive to KV-cache quantization and provides `--kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers` to leave chosen layers at native dtype while the rest use the quantized dtype.
The vLLM skip flag accepts layer-type names (`sliding_window`) or explicit layer indices (e.g. `0 1 23`), and a `kv_cache_dtype_skip_layers=["sliding_window"]` Python argument.
A downstream port commit message cites upstream per-cache rotation for iSWA (ggml-org#21513), giving gpt-oss-20b separate rotation inputs (attn_inp_k_rot, attn_inp_v_rot) for its base and SWA caches.
Inference: because sliding-window layers hold only a short ring (512 or 1024 tokens), keeping them at fp16 costs little memory, so the exclusion rule trades almost nothing for the layers it protects.

CONTRADICTS kv-cache-quantization-tradeoffs-on-apple-gpus.md (rotation cannot apply to Gemma 4 mixed-precision cache): per-cache iSWA rotation exists upstream, so the attn_rot_k = 0 log in #21394 is a point-in-time build observation, not a design limit.
